thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (AAPL, BADU, TSLA, GPRO)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (AAPL, BADU, TSLA, GPRO)
text:
Shutterstock photo Equities closed lower on Friday as the market tried to digest the mixed earnings results received so far among the FANGs — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ). Strong numbers from Amazon and Google weren’t enough to keep the tech heavy Nasdaq in positive territory.
On Thursday, although its Q2 revenue did come in below Street forecasts, Amazon not only reported better-than-expected earnings, its profit surpassed $2 billion for the first time. Meanwhile, the company’s cash cow AWS cloud platform surged 49% year over year.
If not for the tech slump, Amazon might have achieved the $1 trillion marker. That feat could now be achieved by Apple, if the the iPhone maker can deliver a beat on both the top and bottom lines, while issuing confident guidance. Apple’s performance will be one of several topics the Street will monitor this week. Here are a few more stocks to keep an eye on.
AAPL ( AAPL ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, July 31
Wall Street expects Apple to earn $2.18 per share on revenue of $52.34 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.67 per share on revenue of $45.41 billion.
What to Watch: How many iPhones, particularly the more expensive iPhone X, did Apple sell? In the fiscal Q2 the average selling price of iPhones rose 11% YoY to $728, driving Apple Q2 revenue to $61.1 billion, up 16% year over year, while profits soared 25%. As it stands, iPhone revenue now accounts for 62% of total sales. Will this be the quarter that Services revenue, which has a current run rate of $33.4 billion and includes Apple Music, the App Store and Apple Pay, take a bigger step forward?
Baidu ( BIDU ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, July 31
Wall Street expects Baidu to earn $2.61 per share on revenue of $4.03 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $2.52 per share on revenue of $3.29 billion.
What to Watch: The company’s increased investments in its core search business and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, while divesting non-core business, continues to pay off. Last quarter crushed not only analysts revenue and earnings estimates, but also its own forecasts, reporting revenue of $3.33 billion (up 31% YoY), while adjusted EPS surged 133% YoY to $2.60. Investors will be watching closely to see if Baidu’s impressive growth rate can continue.
Tesla ( TSLA ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, August 1
Wall Street expects Tesla to report a per-share loss of $2.81 on revenue of $3.97 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when the loss came to $1.33 per share on revenue of $2.79 billion.
What to Watch: Wall Street is now more optimistic that the company is much closer towards meeting its Model 3 production targets. In April the company announced that it produced a first quarter total of 34,494 vehicles, which marked a sequential increased of 40%. The company also then disclosed that (at the time of the announcement) it had produced 2,020 Model 3 cars within the previous seven days. Tesla has set a goal to hit a weekly production rate of 5,000 Model 3 sedans by the end of June. On Wednesday investors will know if Tesla was able to reach that target. And the reaction from its share price will reveal whether the Street approves.
GoPro ( GPRO ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, August 2
Wall Street expects GoPro to report a per-share loss of 22 cents on revenue of $270.23 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when the loss came to 9 cents per share on revenue of $296.53 million.
What to Watch: Shares of action-camera maker are down 21% so far in 2018, owing to a more than 7% revenue decline in the first quarter. Meanwhile, increased competition have hurt gross margin, and net income for the past three years. During which the stock has lost some 90% of its value. Will this be the quarter that shows the company can turn its business around? With both the Karma drone and the media business defunct GoPro must figure out a way to diversify its revenue for long-term survival.
